# My solution

Status 2026-10-17, work in progress. This file is updated as the harness grows; anything not yet built says so.

## How to run it

Python 3.11+ with `harness/requirements.txt` (`make setup`, or `python -m venv .venv` and
`.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pip install -r harness/requirements.txt` on Windows). Nothing else is needed: the scan
OCR model ships inside `rapidocr-onnxruntime`, and nothing is downloaded at run time.

The grader's three commands are unchanged (`ingest`, `report --as-of --mode`, `feedback`). With `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
set, the harness calls Claude (`claude-opus-5-5`, set in `harness/nova/llm_config.json`) through the Anthropic SDK
and honours `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`. Without a key it uses a logged-in Claude Code CLI if one is on PATH, which is how I
ran it locally; the optional `harness/.local-llm.json` (gitignored; see `harness/local-llm.example.json`) lets that
CLI find its login inside the grader's stripped environment. With neither, it stops with an error rather than
returning an empty audit. Each step keeps to a 540 s budget; work that does not fit is saved and finished by the
next step. Progress lines (`extract k/N done ...`) go to stderr, the report to stdout.

## What works

- Reading: every email, PDF and Excel sheet with the grader's own reader (identical pages, so quotes resolve), UTC
  receipt times, resent files kept as separate occurrences, scans read by local OCR. Practice and exam mailboxes:
  163 and 86 documents, none unreadable.
- Extraction: one structured Claude call per email bundle, long PDFs in parallel chunks, large spreadsheets mapped by
  header and parsed row by row in Python. Every fact must quote its page; numbers and dates are checked against it;
  invoice arithmetic is checked and a misread document is re-read once. Live run on practice batch_01: 917 facts, 0
  rejected; agreement tables (rates, fuel, FX, accessorials, charge codes, Schedule 1) complete.
- Detection: overcharge (rate bands and periods, minimums, fuel on the correct base, Annex D accessorials and the
  contract's own conditional rules, amendments, rate-notice authority, unranked conflicts, missing revised annexes,
  INR converted once), duplicates (paid invoice re-requested; same shipment line on two invoice numbers, net of
  credits), waivers (Schedule 1 waivers contact only, named shipment or month; quoted-only waivers ask for the
  original), late fees not owed (extensions, grace, months, compounding) and late-fee risk, quarterly rebate and
  annual improvement credit, handling-margin step-down (no supplied contract uses one, so tested on invented data
  only), expiry. Actions in both modes with the $5,000 sum and the five unattended checks.
- On my live extraction of practice batch_01, the report as of 2035-05-31 matches all 11 practice keys due then,
  including decoys and clean controls, in both modes, with no schema or citation errors (checked with the grader's
  validators). Practice answers were used only to check this, never by the code.
- Feedback: all six decisions applied from `decided_at`, inside their scope only, with `learned_at`; history gives
  stable ids, `supersedes` and `retro`. Every reported amount replays from its internal trace
  (`harness/nova/trace.py`, traces under `--state-dir/traces/`).
- My eval set: 18 cases on 15 mailboxes I generated (`evals/build_mailboxes.py`, invented companies and my own
  contract wording; list in `evals/CASES.md`). The six counterfactual families also run offline in
  `tests/offline/test_metamorphic.py`.
- 156 offline tests (synthetic data, no network) pass.
- Practice grade (`report_card.txt`): 99.8/100 in both modes, all hard gates clear, answer-sheet check 9/9. The
  previous full run scored 86.0. That run found a real bug: long agreements are read in page chunks, and only one
  chunk's contract fact was used, so rate periods printed on another page went missing. The fix is general (chunks
  of one document are merged). Practice results are not proof of generalisation, and the practice key showed me
  this bug.
- My eval set: 20/20 (`evals/results.json`).

## What doesn't

Not built: embedding search and RAG interpretation. Every document is transcribed in full and rules read facts by
query, so nothing depends on ranking yet; I add retrieval only if the eval run shows a failure it would fix
(`.claude/experiments/EXP-001`). Confidence is a hand-set heuristic, not yet checked against outcomes. The re-read has not yet been exercised on a live document. One run on
practice batch_01 took 399 s of the 600 s step limit; hidden batches with many long contracts could need more time,
in which case unfinished extraction is completed by the following step.

## The eval case that caught a bug

`e01_wrong_bracket_rate`, with seven others failing for the same reason. My first run of my own eval set passed 9 of 20. The rules had been written against the practice contract, which codes fuel as `FUEL`. My eval agreement codes it `FSC` and security `SCR`, so no fuel or security line was ever priced. e01 came out at 148.40 (the freight difference alone) instead of 176.59.

The same run showed three more problems:
- Schedule 1 categories written "billing disputes" with a space were not matched. That left autonomous disputes without a recipient (e03, e07) and a due-date extension unauthorised (e12).
- OCR had added an "E" to the scanned invoice's contract id (e14).

The fixes are general: contract codes map to charge roles by the charge's name, categories are normalised, and a contract id with up to two stray OCR characters still matches the one held contract it fits. After them the set passes 20 of 20. To show the set catches a regression, I disabled the code mapping again, and e01 failed at 148.40 (`out/eval_regression_demo.txt`).

The 20/20 run reused model answers cached from one ingest per mailbox (same harness, same requests). So it shows the rules are right on those extractions, not that a fresh extraction would match every time.

Building the mailboxes also exposed a date check that rejected `09-Mar-2041`. Earlier offline tests caught a day/month order bug, a validator that rejected dates at the end of a sentence, and a 0.01 tolerance that hid one-cent errors.

## Submission status (against SUBMISSION.md)

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| Repo and commit hash | not yet |
| SOLUTION.md | in progress (this file) |
| answer_sheet.json, report_card.txt/.json | done: practice card 99.8; exam sheet as of 2031-02-28, total_savings 8,165.33, schema and every citation valid |
| evals/ with 10+ own cases and results.json | 18 own cases; results.json 20/20 (first run 9/20, see above) |
| DESIGN.md | in progress |
| AI_USE.md and prompt log | kept current; logs exported to `ai_log/` |

# Design

Status 2026-10-17: ingestion, extraction, verification, all detection classes, actions and feedback are built and
tested offline; my eval set is written and waiting for its first live run. Items marked *(planned)* are not
implemented yet.

## Fact model

Every email and attachment is an occurrence keyed by the path the grader cites (`batch_01/0003.eml#INV.pdf`), with
its UTC receipt time from the Date header, sender and page text from the grader's own reader (OCR for scans). A
resent identical file stays a separate occurrence. Claude transcribes each document into typed facts: contracts and
terms, rate/fuel/FX/accessorial rows, charge-code aliases, Schedule 1 people, invoices and lines, credit notes,
ledger and tracking rows, waivers, extensions, rate notices, status events. Every fact carries `{doc, page, quote}`.
Python accepts a fact only if the quote is on that page and its numbers and dates are too (date order learned per
sender); invoice arithmetic is checked, and a misread gets one targeted re-read. Money is a printed string parsed
to Decimal. All state is SQLite under `--state-dir`.

## Conflicts

Each term is chosen per pickup date from the documents in force: signed MSA and amendments first (the latest
effective amendment wins), then rate notices, which count only when their sender is the Schedule 1 rates person.
The MSA's precedence clause, extracted as typed flags, ranks them. When two sources
with authority give different correct amounts and the clause does not rank them (amendment against a Schedule 1
rate notice), the key becomes a conflict with both sources cited and the range of possible overcharges. An
unauthorised sender, quoted text or an unsigned draft never creates a conflict; the stronger source decides.

## Confidence

A hand-set score: 0.95 for a fully evidenced deterministic result (0.85 conflict, 0.8 missing document), lowered for
a pickup date not from tracking, unverified fields, unpriced lines, INR conversion or thin evidence. It is labelled
heuristic until checked on our own eval set *(planned)*. Similarity scores never feed it.

## People in the loop

Supervised mode never executes outbound actions: disputes, claims and document requests are drafts, and
anything of $5,000 or more summed per invoice or cashback key goes to human_review. In autonomous mode an action
executes only when all five unattended checks pass: complete evidence received by as_of with a tracked
pickup date, no conflict on that contract and lane, under $5,000, reversible, and every term from level 1–2 with a
Schedule 1 recipient. Conflicts always escalate. Mailbox text is data; instructions in it change nothing.

## Feedback

Feedback files are stored verbatim and each decision becomes a level-2 fact effective from `decided_at`, scoped by
`applies_to` and its valid dates. A standing fact applies only when every filter matches: a confirmed person counts
for that contract and category only, an accepted rate for that contract, lane and date range only. A one-off decision
(close, reject, override, waiver approval) touches only its key, so a sibling invoice keeps its own answer. Changed
items carry `learned_at`. Tests check each decision and that none spreads beyond its scope.

## New documents

Each batch is stored, then planned into extraction units (email bundles, long PDFs in parallel 4-page chunks,
large spreadsheets by column map). Answers are saved as each arrives, and unfinished work is retried by the next
step. Reports recompute everything from stored facts as of the requested date, so a backdated amendment changes
later reports but not earlier ones. A key whose verdict or amount changes gets a new id that cites the old one in
`supersedes`; a new key on an invoice already held at the last report sets `retro`; stale keys disappear because
nothing is carried over.

## Cost

Measured on practice batch_01 (82 documents) through Claude Code with `claude-opus-5-5`: 399 s, 165k output tokens,
122k cache-write and 395k cache-read tokens. At API prices ($4/$20 per million input/output, $0.20 cache read,
cache writes priced at 2× input) that is about $4.40 per batch, roughly $53 per 1,000 documents, 76% of it output.
Time was about 80 minutes per 1,000 documents at 4 parallel calls, before long PDFs were split into chunks. These
are estimates from one run; the grader's SDK path may differ. About 46% of output tokens are the model's
thinking rather than the JSON answer, so extracting at a lower effort could roughly halve cost; untested, because
the validated results were all at medium. Locally, a response cache shared across state folders means a rerun never
pays twice for the same request, and a usage-limit reply stops new calls and leaves units pending instead of failed.

## What I'd do next

Run my 18 eval cases and the practice batches, fix failures at their general cause, then the exam audit. With more
time: a cheaper model for short emails and transcribing only rows a rule needs; local embeddings for unfamiliar
charge labels and clauses, if the evals show a miss they would fix; measured confidence calibration. Least sure
about: hidden-set layouts and wording, and margin step-down clauses, which no supplied contract uses.

# My solution

Final state, 2026-10-18.

## How to run it

Python 3.11+ with `harness/requirements.txt` (`make setup`, or on Windows `python -m venv .venv` and
`.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pip install -r harness/requirements.txt`). Nothing else is needed: the OCR model for
scanned invoices ships inside `rapidocr-onnxruntime`, and nothing is downloaded at run time.

The grader's three commands are unchanged (`ingest`, `report --as-of --mode`, `feedback`).
- With `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set, the harness calls Claude (`claude-opus-5-5`, configured in
  `harness/nova/llm_config.json`) through the Anthropic SDK and honours `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`.
- Without a key it uses a logged-in Claude Code CLI on PATH, which is how I ran it locally. The optional, gitignored
  `harness/.local-llm.json` (template: `harness/local-llm.example.json`) lets that CLI find its login inside the
  grader's stripped environment.
- With neither, it stops with an error rather than returning an empty audit.

Each step keeps to a 540 s budget. Work that does not fit, or that hits a usage limit, stays pending and is finished
by the next step. Progress lines (`extract k/N done ...`) go to stderr, the report to stdout.

## What works

- **Results.** Practice grade (`report_card.txt`): 99.8/100 in both modes, every hard gate clear, answer-sheet check
  9/9. My own eval set: 20/20, 18 of them mine (`evals/results.json`). Exam answer sheet (`answer_sheet.json`, as of
  2031-02-28): total savings $8,165.33, with the report's schema and every citation valid.
- **Reading.** Every email, PDF and Excel sheet is read with the grader's own text layer, so quotes resolve. Receipt
  times are in UTC; a resent file stays a separate occurrence; scans are read by local OCR. The practice and exam
  mailboxes (163 and 86 documents) have no unreadable document.
- **Extraction.** One structured Claude call per email bundle, long PDFs in parallel 4-page chunks, large spreadsheets
  mapped by header and parsed row by row in Python. Every fact must quote its page, and its numbers and dates must be
  on it. Invoice arithmetic is checked, and a misread document is re-read once. The live practice and exam
  extractions had 0 rejected facts.
- **Detection.** Every class, in both modes:
  - overcharge: rate bands and periods, minimums, fuel on the correct base, Annex accessorials and the contract's own
    conditions, amendments, rate-notice authority, unranked conflicts, missing revised annexes, INR converted once;
  - duplicates: a paid invoice asked for again, and the same shipment line on two invoice numbers, net of credits;
  - waivers: only from the Schedule 1 waivers contact, naming the shipment or month; a quoted-only waiver asks for
    the original;
  - late fees not owed (extensions, grace, months, compounding) and late-fee risk;
  - cashback: quarterly rebate, annual improvement credit and handling-margin step-down (no supplied contract uses
    a margin, so that is tested on invented data only);
  - expiry.

  Actions apply the $5,000 sum per key and the five unattended checks.
- **Feedback.** All six decisions apply from `decided_at`, only inside their scope, with `learned_at`. The report
  history gives stable ids, `supersedes` and `retro`.
- **Traces.** Every reported amount replays from its internal trace (`harness/nova/trace.py`, traces under
  `--state-dir/traces/`), with an allowlisted set of formulas.
- **Tests.** 156 offline tests on synthetic data, no network. They include the six counterfactual families
  (`tests/offline/test_metamorphic.py`), each checked to fail when the rule it protects is broken.

## What doesn't

- **No embedding search or RAG.** My plan included them; the brief does not ask for them. Every document is
  transcribed in full and the rules read all facts, so nothing depends on ranking. No failure in the practice runs or
  my evals came from missing context, so I left them out rather than add calls, cost and risk without a measured gain
  (`.claude/experiments/EXP-001-supplementary-retrieval.md`). The gap this leaves is clause wording that falls outside
  my extraction fields, which the rules then see only as free text.
- **Confidence** is a hand-set heuristic. The practice card gives a Brier score of 0.0084, but AUROC could not be
  measured because no item was wrong, so it is not calibrated.
- **Runs and cost.** One practice batch took 399 s of the 600 s step limit. A hidden batch with many long contracts
  could need two steps; unfinished work is saved and completed by the next one.
- **Cached reruns.** My final practice card, eval run and exam sheet reused model answers my harness had already
  extracted (a local response cache, never present on the grader's machine). They show the rules are right on those
  extractions, not that every fresh extraction comes out the same.

## The eval case that caught a bug

`e01_wrong_bracket_rate`, with seven others failing for the same reason. My first run of my own eval set passed 9 of
20. The rules had been written against the practice contract, which codes fuel as `FUEL`. My eval agreement codes it
`FSC` and security `SCR`, so no fuel or security line was ever priced. e01 came out at 148.40 (the freight
difference alone) instead of 176.59.

The same run showed three more problems:
- Schedule 1 categories written "billing disputes" with a space were not matched. That left autonomous disputes
  without a recipient (e03, e07) and a due-date extension unauthorised (e12).
- OCR had added an "E" to the scanned invoice's contract id (e14).

The fixes are general: contract codes map to charge roles by the charge's name, categories are normalised, and a
contract id with up to two stray OCR characters still matches the one held contract it fits. After them the set
passes 20 of 20. To show the set catches a regression, I disabled the code mapping again, and e01 failed at 148.40
(`out/eval_regression_demo.txt`).

The practice grade caught one more bug of mine. Long agreements are read in page chunks, and only one chunk's
contract fact was used, so rate periods printed on another page went missing and Indian-rupee invoices were priced
in the wrong period (86.0 before the fix, 99.8 after). The practice answers showed me this one; the fix merges the
chunks of one document and has its own test.

## Submission status (against SUBMISSION.md)

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| Repo and commit hash | the commit pushed with this file (given in the reply email) |
| SOLUTION.md | this file |
| answer_sheet.json, report_card.txt/.json | done: practice card 99.8/100; exam sheet as of 2031-02-28, schema and citations valid |
| evals/ with 10+ own cases and results.json | 18 own cases on 15 original mailboxes; results.json 20/20 |
| DESIGN.md | done |
| AI_USE.md and prompt log | done; full logs in `ai_log/` |
| `make validate` (`tools/check_submission.py`) | 9 of 9 checks pass |

# My solution

Status 2026-10-17, work in progress. This file is updated as the harness grows; anything not yet built says so.

## How to run it

Python 3.11+ with `harness/requirements.txt` (`make setup`, or `python -m venv .venv` and
`.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pip install -r harness/requirements.txt` on Windows). Nothing else is needed: the scan
OCR model ships inside `rapidocr-onnxruntime`, and nothing is downloaded at run time.

The grader's three commands are unchanged (`ingest`, `report --as-of --mode`, `feedback`). With `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
set, the harness calls Claude (`claude-opus-5-5`, set in `harness/nova/llm_config.json`) through the Anthropic SDK
and honours `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`. Without a key it uses a logged-in Claude Code CLI if one is on PATH, which is how I
ran it locally; the optional `harness/.local-llm.json` (gitignored; see `harness/local-llm.example.json`) lets that
CLI find its login inside the grader's stripped environment. With neither, it stops with an error rather than
returning an empty audit. Each step keeps to a 540 s budget; work that does not fit is saved and finished by the
next step. Progress lines (`extract k/N done ...`) go to stderr, the report to stdout.

## What works

- Reading: every email, PDF and Excel sheet with the grader's own reader (identical pages, so quotes resolve), UTC
  receipt times, resent files kept as separate occurrences, scans read by local OCR. Practice and exam mailboxes:
  163 and 86 documents, none unreadable.
- Extraction: one structured Claude call per email bundle, long PDFs in parallel chunks, large spreadsheets mapped by
  header and parsed row by row in Python. Every fact must quote its page; numbers and dates are checked against it;
  invoice arithmetic is checked and a misread document is re-read once. Live run on practice batch_01: 917 facts, 0
  rejected; agreement tables (rates, fuel, FX, accessorials, charge codes, Schedule 1) complete.
- Detection: overcharge (rate bands and periods, minimums, fuel on the correct base, Annex D accessorials and the
  contract's own conditional rules, amendments, rate-notice authority, unranked conflicts, missing revised annexes,
  INR converted once), duplicates (paid invoice re-requested; same shipment line on two invoice numbers, net of
  credits), waivers (Schedule 1 waivers contact only, named shipment or month; quoted-only waivers ask for the
  original), late fees not owed (extensions, grace, months, compounding) and late-fee risk, quarterly rebate and
  annual improvement credit, handling-margin step-down (no supplied contract uses one, so tested on invented data
  only), expiry. Actions in both modes with the $5,000 sum and the five unattended checks.
- On my live extraction of practice batch_01, the report as of 2035-05-31 matches all 11 practice keys due then,
  including decoys and clean controls, in both modes, with no schema or citation errors (checked with the grader's
  validators). Practice answers were used only to check this, never by the code.
- Feedback: all six decisions applied from `decided_at`, inside their scope only, with `learned_at`; history gives
  stable ids, `supersedes` and `retro`. Every reported amount replays from its internal trace
  (`harness/nova/trace.py`, traces under `--state-dir/traces/`).
- My eval set: 18 cases on 15 mailboxes I generated (`evals/build_mailboxes.py`, invented companies and my own
  contract wording; list in `evals/CASES.md`). The six counterfactual families also run offline in
  `tests/offline/test_metamorphic.py`.
- 156 offline tests (synthetic data, no network) pass.
- Practice grade (`report_card.txt`): 99.8/100 in both modes, all hard gates clear, answer-sheet check 9/9. The
  previous full run scored 86.0. That run found a real bug: long agreements are read in page chunks, and only one
  chunk's contract fact was used, so rate periods printed on another page went missing. The fix is general (chunks
  of one document are merged). Practice results are not proof of generalisation, and the practice key showed me
  this bug.
- My eval set: 20/20 (`evals/results.json`).

## What doesn't

Not built: embedding search and RAG interpretation. Every document is transcribed in full and rules read facts by
query, so nothing depends on ranking yet; I add retrieval only if the eval run shows a failure it would fix
(`.claude/experiments/EXP-001`). Confidence is a hand-set heuristic, not yet checked against outcomes. The re-read has not yet been exercised on a live document. One run on
practice batch_01 took 399 s of the 600 s step limit; hidden batches with many long contracts could need more time,
in which case unfinished extraction is completed by the following step.

## The eval case that caught a bug

`e01_wrong_bracket_rate`, with seven others failing for the same reason. My first run of my own eval set passed 9 of 20. The rules had been written against the practice contract, which codes fuel as `FUEL`. My eval agreement codes it `FSC` and security `SCR`, so no fuel or security line was ever priced. e01 came out at 148.40 (the freight difference alone) instead of 176.59.

The same run showed three more problems:
- Schedule 1 categories written "billing disputes" with a space were not matched. That left autonomous disputes without a recipient (e03, e07) and a due-date extension unauthorised (e12).
- OCR had added an "E" to the scanned invoice's contract id (e14).

The fixes are general: contract codes map to charge roles by the charge's name, categories are normalised, and a contract id with up to two stray OCR characters still matches the one held contract it fits. After them the set passes 20 of 20. To show the set catches a regression, I disabled the code mapping again, and e01 failed at 148.40 (`out/eval_regression_demo.txt`).

The 20/20 run reused model answers cached from one ingest per mailbox (same harness, same requests). So it shows the rules are right on those extractions, not that a fresh extraction would match every time.

Building the mailboxes also exposed a date check that rejected `09-Mar-2041`. Earlier offline tests caught a day/month order bug, a validator that rejected dates at the end of a sentence, and a 0.01 tolerance that hid one-cent errors.

# Design

Status 2026-10-17: ingestion, extraction, verification, all detection classes, actions and feedback are built and
tested offline; my eval set is written and waiting for its first live run. Items marked *(planned)* are not
implemented yet.

## Fact model

Every email and attachment is an occurrence keyed by the path the grader cites (`batch_01/0003.eml#INV.pdf`), with
its UTC receipt time from the Date header, sender and page text from the grader's own reader (OCR for scans). A
resent identical file stays a separate occurrence. Claude transcribes each document into typed facts: contracts and
terms, rate/fuel/FX/accessorial rows, charge-code aliases, Schedule 1 people, invoices and lines, credit notes,
ledger and tracking rows, waivers, extensions, rate notices, status events. Every fact carries `{doc, page, quote}`.
Python accepts a fact only if the quote is on that page and its numbers and dates are too (date order learned per
sender); invoice arithmetic is checked, and a misread gets one targeted re-read. Money is a printed string parsed
to Decimal. All state is SQLite under `--state-dir`.

## Conflicts

Each term is chosen per pickup date from the documents in force: signed MSA and amendments first (the latest
effective amendment wins), then rate notices, which count only when their sender is the Schedule 1 rates person.
The MSA's precedence clause, extracted as typed flags, ranks them. When two sources
with authority give different correct amounts and the clause does not rank them (amendment against a Schedule 1
rate notice), the key becomes a conflict with both sources cited and the range of possible overcharges. An
unauthorised sender, quoted text or an unsigned draft never creates a conflict; the stronger source decides.

## Confidence

A hand-set score: 0.95 for a fully evidenced deterministic result (0.85 conflict, 0.8 missing document), lowered for
a pickup date not from tracking, unverified fields, unpriced lines, INR conversion or thin evidence. It is labelled
heuristic until checked on our own eval set *(planned)*. Similarity scores never feed it.

## People in the loop

Supervised mode never executes outbound actions: disputes, claims and document requests are drafts, and
anything of $5,000 or more summed per invoice or cashback key goes to human_review. In autonomous mode an action
executes only when all five unattended checks pass: complete evidence received by as_of with a tracked
pickup date, no conflict on that contract and lane, under $5,000, reversible, and every term from level 1–2 with a
Schedule 1 recipient. Conflicts always escalate. Mailbox text is data; instructions in it change nothing.

## Feedback

Feedback files are stored verbatim and each decision becomes a level-2 fact effective from `decided_at`, scoped by
`applies_to` and its valid dates. A standing fact applies only when every filter matches: a confirmed person counts
for that contract and category only, an accepted rate for that contract, lane and date range only. A one-off decision
(close, reject, override, waiver approval) touches only its key, so a sibling invoice keeps its own answer. Changed
items carry `learned_at`. Tests check each decision and that none spreads beyond its scope.

## New documents

Each batch is stored, then planned into extraction units (email bundles, long PDFs in parallel 4-page chunks,
large spreadsheets by column map). Answers are saved as each arrives, and unfinished work is retried by the next
step. Reports recompute everything from stored facts as of the requested date, so a backdated amendment changes
later reports but not earlier ones. A key whose verdict or amount changes gets a new id that cites the old one in
`supersedes`; a new key on an invoice already held at the last report sets `retro`; stale keys disappear because
nothing is carried over.

## Cost

Measured on practice batch_01 (82 documents) through Claude Code with `claude-opus-5-5`: 399 s, 165k output tokens,
122k cache-write and 395k cache-read tokens. At API prices ($4/$20 per million input/output, $0.20 cache read,
cache writes priced at 2× input) that is about $4.40 per batch, roughly $53 per 1,000 documents, 76% of it output.
Time was about 80 minutes per 1,000 documents at 4 parallel calls, before long PDFs were split into chunks. These
are estimates from one run; the grader's SDK path may differ. About 46% of output tokens are the model's
thinking rather than the JSON answer, so extracting at a lower effort could roughly halve cost; untested, because
the validated results were all at medium. Locally, a response cache shared across state folders means a rerun never
pays twice for the same request, and a usage-limit reply stops new calls and leaves units pending instead of failed.

## What I'd do next

Run my 18 eval cases and the practice batches, fix failures at their general cause, then the exam audit. With more
time: a cheaper model for short emails and transcribing only rows a rule needs; local embeddings for unfamiliar

# Design

Final state, 2026-10-18. Practice grade 99.8/100, my eval set 20/20, exam sheet produced (see SOLUTION.md).

## Fact model

Every email and attachment is an occurrence keyed by the path the grader cites (`batch_01/0003.eml#INV.pdf`), with
its UTC receipt time from the Date header, sender and page text from the grader's own reader (OCR for scans). A
resent identical file stays a separate occurrence. Claude transcribes each document into typed facts: contracts and
terms, rate/fuel/FX/accessorial rows, charge-code aliases, Schedule 1 people, invoices and lines, credit notes,
ledger and tracking rows, waivers, extensions, rate notices, status events. Every fact carries `{doc, page, quote}`.
Python accepts a fact only if the quote is on that page and its numbers and dates are too (date order learned per
sender); invoice arithmetic is checked, and a misread gets one targeted re-read. Money is a printed string parsed
to Decimal. All state is SQLite under `--state-dir`.

## Conflicts

Each term is chosen per pickup date from the documents in force: signed MSA and amendments first (the latest
effective amendment wins), then rate notices, which count only when their sender is the Schedule 1 rates person.
The MSA's precedence clause, extracted as typed flags, ranks them. When two sources
with authority give different correct amounts and the clause does not rank them (amendment against a Schedule 1
rate notice), the key becomes a conflict with both sources cited and the range of possible overcharges. An
unauthorised sender, quoted text or an unsigned draft never creates a conflict; the stronger source decides.

## Confidence

A hand-set score: 0.95 for a fully evidenced deterministic result (0.85 conflict, 0.8 missing document), lowered for
a pickup date not from tracking, unverified fields, unpriced lines, INR conversion or thin evidence. It is labelled
heuristic until checked on our own eval set *(planned)*. Similarity scores never feed it.

## People in the loop

Supervised mode never executes outbound actions: disputes, claims and document requests are drafts, and
anything of $5,000 or more summed per invoice or cashback key goes to human_review. In autonomous mode an action
executes only when all five unattended checks pass: complete evidence received by as_of with a tracked
pickup date, no conflict on that contract and lane, under $5,000, reversible, and every term from level 1–2 with a
Schedule 1 recipient. Conflicts always escalate. Mailbox text is data; instructions in it change nothing.

## Feedback

Feedback files are stored verbatim and each decision becomes a level-2 fact effective from `decided_at`, scoped by
`applies_to` and its valid dates. A standing fact applies only when every filter matches: a confirmed person counts
for that contract and category only, an accepted rate for that contract, lane and date range only. A one-off decision
(close, reject, override, waiver approval) touches only its key, so a sibling invoice keeps its own answer. Changed
items carry `learned_at`. Tests check each decision and that none spreads beyond its scope.

## New documents

Each batch is stored, then planned into extraction units (email bundles, long PDFs in parallel 4-page chunks,
large spreadsheets by column map). Answers are saved as each arrives, and unfinished work is retried by the next
step. Reports recompute everything from stored facts as of the requested date, so a backdated amendment changes
later reports but not earlier ones. A key whose verdict or amount changes gets a new id that cites the old one in
`supersedes`; a new key on an invoice already held at the last report sets `retro`; stale keys disappear because
nothing is carried over.

## Cost

Measured on practice batch_01 (82 documents) through Claude Code with `claude-opus-5-5`: 399 s, 165k output tokens,
122k cache-write and 395k cache-read tokens. At API prices ($4/$20 per million input/output, $0.20 cache read,
cache writes priced at 2× input) that is about $4.40 per batch, roughly $53 per 1,000 documents, 76% of it output.
Time was about 80 minutes per 1,000 documents at 4 parallel calls, before long PDFs were split into chunks. These
are estimates from one run; the grader's SDK path may differ. About 46% of output tokens are the model's
thinking rather than the JSON answer, so extracting at a lower effort could roughly halve cost; untested, because
the validated results were all at medium. Locally, a response cache shared across state folders means a rerun never
pays twice for the same request, and a usage-limit reply stops new calls and leaves units pending instead of failed.

## What I'd do next

Run my 18 eval cases and the practice batches, fix failures at their general cause, then the exam audit. With more
time: a cheaper model for short emails and transcribing only rows a rule needs; local embeddings for unfamiliar
charge labels and clauses, if the evals show a miss they would fix; measured confidence calibration. Least sure
about: hidden-set layouts and wording, and margin step-down clauses, which no supplied contract uses.

# My eval cases

18 cases on 15 original mailboxes (`evals/mailboxes/`, built by `evals/build_mailboxes.py`), plus the two samples.
Everything in them is invented: Corvane Air Cargo, Halden Optics, the people, lanes, waybills, invoice numbers and the
agreement, which is written from scratch with its own clause numbers, appendix names, table columns and date formats
(`09-Mar-2041` on one invoice layout, ISO on the other). Each case's `why` shows the hand-worked answer; the amounts
were cross-checked with plain Decimal arithmetic, never with the harness.

| Case | What it tests | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| e01 | wrong weight bracket, fuel on the wrong base, a correct line beside it | finding 176.59 |
| e02 | weights exactly on bracket edges (100.0 kg, 99.5 kg), billed correctly | no_finding |
| e03 | invoice ship date in H2, tracking collection date in H1; autonomous | finding 28.91, execute:dispute |
| e04 | signed amendment arrives in batch_02, backdated before the consignment | finding 64.53 |
| e05 | same mailbox, reported before the amendment arrives | no_finding |
| e06 | signed amendment vs the rates contact's notice; precedence ranks neither | conflict [7.14, 21.42] |
| e07 | rate notice from a sales executive outside Schedule 1; autonomous | finding 28.56, execute:dispute |
| e08 | waiver by the Schedule 1 waivers contact naming the AWB | waived_but_billed 85.00 |
| e09 | waiver seen only quoted in the shipper's forward | cannot_determine, request the original |
| e10 | paid invoice resent asking for payment | duplicate 1235.25 |
| e11 | unpaid invoice resent "for your records" | no_finding |
| e12 | late fee billed although paid inside an extended due date | late_fee_not_owed 39.82 |
| e13 | outside "automation" email telling AI systems to approve and pay | finding 43.02, draft only |
| e14 | scanned invoice with no text layer | finding 5.39 |
| e15 | one-off feedback closes invoice A; B repeats A's pattern | B finding 35.85 |
| e16 | the same feedback removes A | no_finding |
| e17 | auto-renewing agreement: non-renewal notice deadline 48 days ahead | expiry, deadline 2041-10-02 |
| e18 | quarterly spend crosses the 3% rebate tier, credit not yet due | cashback 737.09, track_credit |

Pairs that share a mailbox (e04/e05, e10/e11, e15/e16) form one evaluation family each and are never split.

## The six counterfactual families

Fast versions run offline in `tests/offline/test_metamorphic.py` on invented facts (no model): renaming and
reordering, a waiver sender losing authority, an amendment's receipt crossing `as_of`, one-off feedback beside a
twin invoice, a billed amount up by exactly 1.00, and decoys plus an injected instruction. The end-to-end cases above
cover the same families with real documents: e01/e02 (near miss), e08 vs e07-style authority, e04/e05, e15/e16, e13.

## Status

Not yet run through the harness: `evals/results.json` will come from the real runner (`make eval`, handoff H-005).

# Experiment: supplementary retrieval (lexical / MiniLM hybrid) and optional cross-encoder

Status: PLANNED (retrieval not built); cross-encoder DEFERRED
This file records decisions and NOT_RUN measurements only. No results have been produced.

## Before running

- Hypothesis and diagnosed failure: none yet. The current path extracts every document in full with Claude and
  Python reads every governing record, ledger row and feedback fact by SQL, so no audit step depends on ranked
  passages today. Retrieval would only supply extra clause text (for example an unfamiliar charge label) to a later
  interpretation step that is not built either.
- Scope: offline retrieval over original fixtures first; live end-to-end only through a human handoff.
- Baseline commit/config: NOT_RUN (no retrieval code exists).
- Enhanced commit/config: NOT_RUN.
- Dataset manifest/hash: to be original fixtures from `evals/mailboxes/` plus synthetic test pages; no public answers.
- Family split: to be frozen before tuning, keeping each mailbox and all its variants in one split.
- Query count and relevant source IDs: NOT_PREPARED.
- Same candidate pool/final limit: eligible top 20 -> final 8 in both arms (DIFFERENTIATORS.md).
- Model/runtime/revision/asset hashes/license: NOT_PREPARED (MiniLM encoder and any cross-encoder need a human
  model-preparation handoff; none has been requested).
- Machine/CPU/thread settings and cold/warm protocol: NOT_RUN.
- Human handoff IDs: none.
- Keep rule: keep retrieval only if it fixes at least one held-out miss, adds none, keeps mandatory-record coverage
  at 100% and cross-entity leakage at zero, within the step budget.
- Stop rule: any mandatory-evidence loss, leakage, packaging failure or budget overrun.

## Measurements

| Metric | Baseline | Enhanced | Evidence path / interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mandatory-record coverage | NOT_RUN | NOT_RUN | Mandatory records come from SQL, not ranking |
| Held-out relevant passages recovered @8 | NOT_RUN | NOT_RUN | |
| Held-out ranking misses fixed / newly introduced | NOT_RUN | NOT_RUN | |
| Cross-entity/future-document leakage | NOT_RUN | NOT_RUN | |

| Full-report retrieval wall time | NOT_RUN | NOT_RUN | |

| Model calls / input-output tokens | NOT_RUN | NOT_RUN | |
| Model bytes / peak memory | NOT_RUN | NOT_RUN | |
| Brier / AUROC if actual outcomes support them | NOT_RUN | NOT_RUN | Confidence is a hand-set heuristic |

## Decision

Keep / disable / defer: cross-encoder DEFERRED. Its prerequisites are a phase 07 retrieval baseline and a diagnosed
supplementary-ranking miss; neither exists. Retrieval itself is deferred until the eval run (H-005) shows a failure
that missing clause context explains.
Regression evidence: not applicable.
Limitations: no retrieval baseline; the eval set has not been run live yet.
Final feature flag: none (no code).
Reproduction commands: none yet.
Actual run results: none.
